content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves D5 vs C5 by treating the Isaiah 7:14 rows and the open sense of the sign as decisive, so it is assessing the kind of chain collision K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse — one reading forbids deciding the collision from the open sense of Isaiah 7:14 alone; the other permits that as part of chain support.", "why": "The judge finds D5 underdetermined because the sign's sense remains open, which is a verse-level underdetermination rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing as K-C requires."}
